learning: If s-bend line losses fall but oval finish rate drops, the gain increase is too strong; return kp to 2.5. If s-bend max_error stays at the 0.06 floor with low oscillation, the next lever is turn authority, through a narrower track or higher kp, rather than more look-ahead.
notes: Accepts the Builder's y 0.07 look-ahead with wheel_track 0.10. Raises kp to 2.8 and kd to 0.45 to add s-bend turn authority and damp the longer sensing lag.
rationale: Iteration 1 (score 389.4) raised the oval to 19 of 20 finishes with mean rms 0.015, so the 0.06 m look-ahead and 0.10 m track work for the oval. The s-bend still left the line on all 20 trials, with progress 0.43, max_error at the 0.0624 m floor, and 1.0 line loss per run. Steering oscillation stayed low on every track (0.23, 0.23, 0.27), so the failure is late reaction, not jitter. The slalom still lost the line 1.75 times per run with progress 0.18. The Builder's proposal moves the sensors to y 0.07, which is within the 0.08 limit, and keeps wheel_track at 0.10, so I accept the geometry as proposed. Because the longer look-ahead adds sensing lag, I raise kp from 2.5 to 2.8 to add turn authority on the s-bend. The narrow track already gives 1.2x turn rate per unit of wheel difference, and oscillation is low enough to absorb a modest gain increase. I raise kd from 0.4 to 0.45 to damp the extra lag. ki stays at 0.05, base_speed stays at 1.5 (the oval finished in 1.91 s, so there is time margin), and line_loss stays last_direction, since the robot should keep turning the way it was going when the tape leaves the sensors. Expected result, not measured: s-bend line_loss_events below 1.0 and progress above 0.43, with the slalom loss count falling from 1.75. The risk is that the higher kp or the longer look-ahead overshoots on the oval, which would show as a rise in oval max_error with the finish rate falling below 0.9. The observation request asks for per-track max_error and line losses so both cases can be told apart.
